items.title: Disk-like capped gropes of height one and one-half

references.title: Stefan Behrens et al., The Disc Embedding Theorem

items.statement: Use the framed four-dimensional block and stage conventions for gropes in the cited definitions. A **capped grope** is a staged thickening whose bottom surface stage is joined along curves in a symplectic basis to higher surface stages, with the final tip circles capped by framed immersed disks. A **disk-like capped grope** has one connected bottom surface stage with exactly one attaching circle. Its **height** is the number of successive surface stages on each side of the symplectic basis, with caps terminating the stages. A disk-like capped grope has **height one and one-half**, written $1.5$, when its two sides have heights $(1,0)$ or $(0,1)$ in the asymmetric convention; equivalently, one half of the first-stage basis has one additional surface stage and the other half is capped immediately. The **attaching region** is the framed solid-torus neighborhood of the single attaching circle. For an immersed disk, a **double-point loop** is the image of a path in the domain disk joining the two preimages of a transverse self-intersection. In the disk-embedding property for an input capped grope, this loop is read as the corresponding element of the grope's fundamental group; choosing a basing path from the grope basepoint fixes that based element.

items.title: Freedman disk-embedding data

references.title: Michael H. Freedman and Frank Quinn, Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: §1.7, intersection and self-intersection numbers, printed pp.20–23; §5.1, Theorems 5.1A–5.1B, printed pp.85–87

references.title: Stefan Behrens et al., The Disc Embedding Theorem
references.locator: Chapter 11, intersection numbers and the relative disc-embedding statement

references.title: Mark Powell, Arunima Ray and Peter Teichner, The 4-dimensional disc embedding theorem and dual spheres
references.locator: Selecta Mathematica 31:80 (2025), Theorem A, PDF p.3; Section 3, PDF p.13 (extending Whitney framing); Remark 6.3, PDF pp.22–23 (prescribed boundary framing and its relative extension obstruction)

items.statement: Let $X$ be a compact connected oriented topological $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary, let $x_0\in X$, and put $G=\pi_1(X,x_0)$. A **finite relative disk-embedding datum** consists of proper generic immersions $f_i:(D^2,S^1)\looparrowright(X,\partial X)$, $1\le i\le n$, whose boundary circles are embedded and pairwise disjoint, together with framed generic immersions $g_i:S^2\looparrowright\operatorname{int}X$ that are algebraically dual to the disks. A topological generic immersion has the local models of a smooth generic immersion: at a point with one inverse image its image sheet is locally flat, with a proper half-space chart at boundary points in which the disk is a half-plane and its boundary lies on the ambient boundary, and each of its finitely many self-double points has exactly two preimages and the coordinate-plane model $\mathbb R^2\times\{0\}$ and $\{0\}\times\mathbb R^2$ in a chart of $X$. All mutual intersections among the disk and sphere maps are also required to be finite and transverse, so the equivariant intersection sums below are finite. Proper means that the inverse image of $\partial X$ is exactly the domain boundary. Each disk $f_i$ is supplied with a specified normal framing along $S^1$, equivalently the framing of its boundary attaching solid torus; this boundary framing is part of the datum and need not extend over $D^2$. Each sphere $g_i$ is supplied with a trivialization of its normal microbundle over $S^2$. Choose paths from $x_0$ to the immersed surfaces and orient the surfaces. Each transverse intersection $p$ of two surfaces contributes $\epsilon(p)g_p$ to $\lambda$, where $\epsilon(p)\in\{1,-1\}$ compares their induced local orientation with the chosen orientation of $X$, and $g_p\in G$ is the loop that travels along the chosen path to the first surface, then to $p$, and returns along the second surface and its chosen path. Thus $\lambda$ is a signed equivariant intersection sum in $\mathbb Z[G]$. Wall's self-intersection sum $\mu$ is the signed sum over self-double points in $\mathbb Z[G]/\langle g-g^{-1}:g\in G\rangle$, because interchanging the two sheets replaces a label by its inverse. The relative normal Euler (boundary-framing) obstruction of $f_i$ is zero precisely when its specified boundary framing extends over $D^2$; the datum does not assume that it vanishes. The spheres are **algebraically dual** when $\lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij}$, $\lambda(g_i,g_j)=0$ for every $i,j$, and $\mu(g_i)=0$ for every $i$. The disk data are **algebraically unobstructed** when also $\lambda(f_i,f_j)=0$ for $i\ne j$ and $\mu(f_i)=0$ for every $i$.

items.title: Good fundamental groups for the disk-embedding theorem

references.title: Stefan Behrens et al., The Disc Embedding Theorem
references.locator: Definition 12.12 and Chapter 19, printed pp.180–181 and 273–282

items.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a group. Say that $\Gamma$ is **good for the Freedman disk-embedding theorem** when it has the $\pi_1$-null disk property: for every disk-like capped grope $G^c$ of height $1.5$ with a chosen basepoint and every homomorphism $\phi:\pi_1(G^c)\to\Gamma$, there is a proper framed generic immersion $d:D^2\looparrowright G^c$ of a disk into the grope's actual four-dimensional framed block. Its boundary is the core attaching circle, with the normal framing specified by the attaching solid-torus neighborhood, and each double-point loop of $d$, regarded after basing as an element of $\pi_1(G^c)$, is sent to the identity by $\phi$. This definition of a good group is a hypothesis on $\Gamma$; it does not assert that any particular group is good.

items.title: Capped-grope skyscraper construction and standardness for good-group disk data

references.title: Michael H. Freedman and Frank Quinn, Topology of 4-Manifolds

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be an oriented topological $4$-manifold with boundary, and let $V\subset X$ be a connected relatively open neighborhood endowed with a specified smooth structure compatible with its smooth boundary collar and the given framed disk data, whose specified boundary collars and normal framings are smooth in this structure. Assume $\pi_1(V)$ is good for disk embedding. Let $f_i:(D^2,S^1)\looparrowright(V,V\cap\partial X)$ be a finite proper smooth generic disk datum with pairwise disjoint embedded framed boundaries, and framed smooth immersed spheres $g_i$ satisfying $\lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij}$, $\lambda(g_i,g_j)=0$, $\mu(g_i)=0$, $\lambda(f_i,f_j)=0$ for $i\ne j$, and $\mu(f_i)=0$, computed in $\mathbb Z[\pi_1(V)]$.

There is a finite family of proper framed one-story capped-grope towers in $V$, of first-story height at least four, whose attaching regions are the Whitney circles for a regular homotopy of the $f_i$. Their bodies extend to embedded convergent skyscraper pinched neighborhoods, each with a relative standard-two-handle parameterization preserving its attaching solid torus and framing. The corresponding embedded framed Whitney disks give pairwise disjoint proper locally flat disks $\bar f_i$ homotopic to $f_i$ rel boundary and framing. They carry product normal neighborhoods supplied by this construction and framed immersed geometric duals $\bar g_i$ homotopic in $V$ to $g_i$.

In particular one may take $V=X$ when $X$ and the given maps, boundary collars and framings are smooth. No existence of a smoothing of a general topological neighborhood is asserted. The towers are capped-grope skyscrapers; an unrestricted Casson-handle construction is not assumed.

items.title: Standardized Casson towers yield locally flat disks

references.title: Michael H. Freedman and Frank Quinn, Topology of 4-Manifolds
Stefan Behrens et al., The Disc Embedding Theorem
references.locator: Chapters 17–18 and 24–28: height raising, embedding, and standardness

items.statement: Let $X$ be a compact oriented topological $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary. A **kinky handle** is a standard $2$-handle whose core disk has finitely many transverse self-plumbings; a **framed Casson-handle tower** is a nested sequence of such stages in which each self-plumbing point of one stage is replaced by a framed kinky handle at the next stage, with the attaching regions matching the preceding stage. Suppose a finite family of these tower $4$-neighborhoods is embedded pairwise disjointly in $X$, with attaching circles in $\partial X$, and carries the algebraic dual data of a disk-embedding datum. If each embedded tower has a homeomorphism of pairs to the standard open $2$-handle $D^2\times\mathbb R^2$ that takes its specified framed attaching region, including its core circle and normal-framing class, to the standard attaching region $S^1\times\mathbb R^2$ with its standard framing, then the inverse images of the cores $D^2\times\{0\}$ form a pairwise disjoint family of locally flat properly embedded disks in $X$, with the prescribed framed boundary circles.

items.title: The infinite cyclic group is good for disk embedding

references.title: Michael H. Freedman and Frank Quinn, Topology of 4-Manifolds

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The infinite cyclic group $\mathbb Z$ is good for the Freedman disk-embedding theorem, in the sense of the $\pi_1$-null disk property defined for a good fundamental group.

items.title: Freedman disk-embedding theorem for good groups

references.title: Michael H. Freedman and Frank Quinn, Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: §5.1, Theorems 5.1A–5.1B, printed pp.85–87

references.title: Stefan Behrens et al., The Disc Embedding Theorem
references.locator: Chapter 11, disc-embedding theorem statement and intersection hypotheses

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a compact connected oriented smooth $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary and good fundamental group $G=\pi_1(X)$. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_n:(D^2,S^1)\looparrowright(X,\partial X)$ be proper generic immersed disks with pairwise disjoint embedded boundary circles. Suppose they admit framed immersed algebraically dual spheres $g_1,\ldots,g_n$ with $\lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij}$, $\lambda(g_i,g_j)=0$, and $\mu(g_i)=0$, and suppose $\lambda(f_i,f_j)=0$ for $i\ne j$ and $\mu(f_i)=0$ for all $i$, in the equivariant intersection conventions of the disk-embedding data definition. Then the disks are homotopic rel boundary, preserving the boundary framings, to pairwise disjoint locally flat properly embedded disks in $X$.

items.title: The reverse-mirror Seifert matrix is the negative original

references.title: Arunima Ray, Slice Knots and Knot Concordance
references.locator: §1.1, mirror and reverse conventions, printed p.2

items.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with a Seifert surface $F$ and ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$, using $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ for the positive-push Seifert matrix. Let $K^\dagger$ be the reverse mirror defined by the fixed orientation-reversing reflection followed by reversal of the knot orientation, and use the image basis on the reflected surface. The Seifert matrix of $K^\dagger$ in that basis is $-V$.

items.title: S-equivalence of integral Seifert forms

references.title: Stavros Garoufalidis and Peter Teichner, On Knots with Trivial Alexander Polynomial
references.locator: §3, Definition 3.2 and the matrix of an algebraic tube addition, printed pp.3–4

references.title: H. F. Trotter, On S-equivalence of Seifert Matrices
references.locator: Inventiones Mathematicae 20 (1973), pp.173–207

items.statement:
Let $V$ be an integral Seifert matrix in the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Two integral Seifert forms are **S-equivalent** when they are related by a finite sequence of integral unimodular basis changes and algebraic tube additions or their inverses. A basis change replaces $V$ by $P^T V P$ for $P\in\operatorname{GL}_m(\mathbb Z)$. A tube addition replaces $V$ by
$$\begin{pmatrix} V&0&\rho\\ 0&0&1\\ \rho^T&0&0 \end{pmatrix},\qquad \rho\in\mathbb Z^m,$$
where the two new basis elements are the short and long curves of the added tube. The **empty Seifert form** is the unique bilinear form on the zero module, represented by the $0\times0$ matrix.

items.title: An Alexander-one Seifert form is S-equivalent to the empty form

references.title: Stavros Garoufalidis and Peter Teichner, On Knots with Trivial Alexander Polynomial
references.locator: Lemma 4.2, printed pp.5–6

references.title: H. F. Trotter, On S-equivalence of Seifert Matrices
references.locator: *Inventiones Mathematicae* 20 (1973), pp.173–207; proof not yet inspected completely

items.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K(t)\doteq1$, where $\doteq$ denotes equality up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$. For every Seifert surface $F$ of $K$ and every integral Seifert matrix $V$ of $F$ in the positive-push convention, the form represented by $V$ is S-equivalent over $\mathbb Z$ to the empty Seifert form.

items.title: An Alexander-one knot has a trivial Alexander basis

references.title: Stavros Garoufalidis and Peter Teichner, On Knots with Trivial Alexander Polynomial
references.locator: Definition 4.1 and Lemma 4.2, printed pp.5–6

references.title: H. F. Trotter, On S-equivalence of Seifert Matrices
references.locator: The S-equivalence input invoked in Lemma 4.2; proof not yet reconstructed locally

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with $\Delta_K(t)\doteq1$, where $\doteq$ denotes equality up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$. Then $K$ has a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface $F$ and an ordered geometric basis, represented by embedded simple closed curves $s_1,\ldots,s_g,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_g$ for $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, such that $s_i\cdot_Fs_j=0=\ell_i\cdot_F\ell_j$ and $s_i\cdot_F\ell_j=\delta_{ij}$, and the Seifert matrix in this basis has block form
$$V=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_g+U\\U^T&W\end{pmatrix},$$
where $U$ is strictly upper triangular and $W$ is symmetric with zero diagonal. Such a geometric symplectic basis and block matrix are called a trivial Alexander basis.

items.title: An Alexander-one knot supplies good-group disk-embedding data

references.title: Stavros Garoufalidis and Peter Teichner, On Knots with Trivial Alexander Polynomial
references.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.1 and the complete Alexander-one construction, printed pp.12–13

references.title: Michael H. Freedman and Frank Quinn, Topology of 4-Manifolds
references.locator: §1.7, printed pp.20–23, for the explicit intersection/framing identities; §5.1 for the disk-data convention

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with $\Delta_K(t)\doteq1$. There is a connected compact smooth Seifert surface $F$ with a geometric symplectic basis $s_1,\ldots,s_g,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_g$ whose positive-push matrix is
$$V=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_g+U\\ U^T&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad U\text{ strictly upper triangular}.$$
Place $F$ on the unit sphere in the literal radius-$3/2$ ball and join its boundary to the outer copy of $K$ by the radial product collar, rounding the inner junction away from that outer collar. Write $\Sigma$ for this proper surface. Its actual smooth normal thickening can be chosen so that the rounded complement
$$N=B^4_{3/2}\setminus\operatorname{int}\nu\Sigma$$
is compact, connected and smooth, with $\pi_1(N)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by the positive normal meridian of $\Sigma$.

The fixed negative normal pushoffs of the short curves give disjoint framed circles $\delta_i\subset\partial N$. They bound proper framed smooth generic disks $\Delta_i$ in $N$ admitting framed smooth immersed spheres $f_i$ such that
$$\lambda(\Delta_i,f_j)=\delta_{ij},\quad \lambda(\Delta_i,\Delta_j)=0\ (i\ne j),\quad \mu(\Delta_i)=0,\quad \lambda(f_i,f_j)=0,\quad\mu(f_i)=0$$
in $\mathbb Z[\mathbb Z]$ with the specified Wall conventions. Along the fixed annuli from $\delta_i$ to $s_i\subset\Sigma$, their boundary framings agree with the normal directions of $s_i$ within $\Sigma$. Thus the data retain the actual ambient ball, complement, attaching circles and compression framings. The group is good when the infinite-cyclic good-group theorem is supplied. For $g=0$ the disk and sphere families are empty and the geometric complement assertion remains valid.

items.title: Alexander polynomial one implies topological sliceness

references.title: Michael H. Freedman and Frank Quinn, Topology of 4-Manifolds
Stavros Garoufalidis and Peter Teichner, On Knots with Trivial Alexander Polynomial
references.locator: Appendix A, complete disk-embedding application, printed pp.12–13

items.statement: Assume full AC. If a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ has Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K(t)\doteq1$, where $\doteq$ denotes equality up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, then there is a locally flat proper embedding $D^2\hookrightarrow B^4$ whose boundary is $K$. Here **topologically slice** means bounding such a locally flat proper disk; the conclusion asserts no smooth slice disk.

title: Freedman’s theorem and topological sliceness — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The square knot is slice despite its nonunit Alexander polynomial

references.title: Arunima Ray, Slice Knots and Knot Concordance
references.locator: §1.1, reverse-mirror ribbon construction, printed pp.4–5

references.title: Dale Rolfsen, Knots and Links
references.locator: §8.A, right-handed trefoil Seifert matrix, printed pp.200–202

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $T$ be the right-handed trefoil and let $S=T\#T^\dagger$ be the square knot in the fixed oriented connected-sum convention. The universal converse assertion “if a knot has nonunit Alexander polynomial, then it is not topologically slice” is false: $S$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in the standard unit four-ball $B^4\subset\mathbb R^4$ whose squared radial function has only index-$0$ and index-$1$ interior critical points, while $\Delta_S(t)\doteq(t^2-t+1)^2$. Here $\doteq$ means equality up to a unit of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$; those units are exactly $\pm t^k$, and the displayed polynomial has nonzero terms in degrees $0$ through $4$, so it is not a unit. A knot is topologically slice when it bounds a locally flat disk in $B^4$, and every smooth proper disk is locally flat. The trefoil itself also has nonunit Alexander polynomial, but this fact alone only places it outside the hypothesis of the Alexander-one sufficient theorem and proves no nonsliceness claim about the trefoil.

items.title: Unknot, trefoil, and positive untwisted Whitehead double cases

references.title: Matthew Hedden and Juanita Pinzón-Caicedo, Satellites of Infinite Rank in the Smooth Concordance Group
references.locator: §5.2.2, Figure 2, printed pp.18–19; $P_0$ is the positive untwisted pattern and $V_0= egin{pmatrix}0&0\-1&-1nd{pmatrix}$

references.locator: Introduction and Appendix A: Alexander-one knots and topological sliceness

references.title: Arunima Ray, Slice Knots and Knot Concordance
references.locator: Definition 1.10, Theorem 1.13, and Figure 8, printed pp.5–6

items.statement: Assume full AC. The unknot has the empty Seifert matrix, Alexander polynomial $1$, and a smooth slice disk. The right-handed trefoil has positive-push matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ and Alexander polynomial $t^2-t+1$, so the Alexander-one theorem gives no conclusion for it and does not prove it nonslice. Let $Wh^+(T)$ denote the satellite of the right-handed trefoil $T$ by the positive-clasped, untwisted Whitehead pattern, embedded using the preferred longitude. This knot has Alexander polynomial $1$; by topologically slice we mean that it bounds a locally flat embedded disk in $B^4$. The established theorem gives that topological conclusion, not a smooth slice disk.
